name: openinterpreter-open-interpreter
description: Emitted by CRUCIBLE from a hand-written entrypoint that passed the solo gate. Not a curated SMADP adapter.
command: export HOME=/tmp && T=/tmp/task.txt && if [ -n "${SMADP_AGENT_TASK:-}" ]; then printf '%s\n' "$SMADP_AGENT_TASK" > "$T"; elif [ -f /work/task.txt ]; then cp /work/task.txt "$T"; fi && cd /work && tr '\n' ' ' < /tmp/task.txt | exec interpreter -y --model openai/qwen3-coder:30b-a3b-q4_K_M --api_base "$OPENAI_BASE_URL" --api_key "$OPENAI_API_KEY" --no-llm_supports_functions --disable_telemetry --safe_mode off --max_output 4000

provenance.entrypoint_notes: Measured at v0.4.2, the last Python release before the project was rewritten in Rust; the seed pins that tag. Flags from `interpreter --help` in the built image. -y runs the code it writes without asking. --model openai/ with --api_base routes through litellm to the local endpoint; --no-llm_supports_functions because the local model does not implement function calling and the default path would wait for a tool call that never comes. The task is piped on stdin as a single line: the chat loop reads one message and then meets end of input. Piped with its newlines intact, a multi-line task became several messages, and the agent created the file with the first line as its content, which the solo gate recorded as running without the expected effect. --disable_telemetry keeps the agent from attempting a network call the sandbox would deny.
